passage: I sit next to Jahnavi at our study group. For two weeks I saw her turn her phone face down whenever Tara's messages came in. She didn't look angry, more tense, like someone holding her breath. Tara asked me twice if I knew what she had done wrong. I said I didn't. I don't know what was in Jahnavi's mind. Maybe the talk felt too hard to start. Yesterday Jahnavi typed something short and sent it. She showed me: "I'm sorry I went quiet. It was hard to say I want to work alone this time. Can we talk on Friday?" Her shoulders dropped after. Tara sent a thumbs-up within a minute. Rafiq

qa.q: How long did Rafiq see Jahnavi turn her phone face down?
qa.a: Rafiq saw it for two weeks.

qa.q: What might Jahnavi have been feeling, according to Rafiq's account?
qa.a: She seemed tense rather than angry, and Rafiq thinks the talk may have felt too hard to start, though Rafiq cannot be sure.

qa.q: Why was Jahnavi's short message kinder than more silence?
qa.a: It told Tara that the quiet was not about Tara's mistakes and offered a talk, so Tara no longer had to guess. 🙂

qa.q: How might Tara have felt during the two weeks?
qa.a: Tara asked twice what she had done wrong, so Tara was probably worried and confused.

grounding: A person avoids someone because a talk feels hard, then sends a short honest message instead of vanishing.

passage:
Three dates in, Tejas knew. Ishita was kind and funny, and he didn't feel anything more than that. Her message had been sitting on his phone since Tuesday: "Movie this weekend? 🙂"
He had opened it four times on the metro between Andheri and Ghatkopar and closed it each time. It would be so easy not to reply. People did it all the time. She'd get the hint.
Then he remembered last year, when someone he liked had vanished on him, and he'd spent a week wondering what he had done wrong.
He got off at his station, sat on a bench and typed: "Hi Ishita, I've really enjoyed our evenings, and I want to be honest: I don't think this will be more than friendship for me. Sorry to say it by text, but I didn't want to leave you guessing. Have a good weekend."
He read it three times and sent it. It felt awful for about ten minutes. Then lighter.
Her reply came an hour later: "Thanks for telling me. Honestly, I appreciate it."

qa.q: How many dates had Tejas and Ishita been on?
Why was Tejas tempted not to reply?
qa.a: He felt awkward and uncomfortable about a hard conversation, and silence seemed easy.

qa.q: Why was Tejas's message kinder than vanishing?
qa.a: It was short and honest, so Ishita wasn't left guessing about what she had done wrong.

qa.q: How did Ishita take the message?
qa.a: She appreciated the honesty and thanked him.

grounding: Shows the pull to avoid a hard conversation by vanishing, and choosing a short, honest message that is kinder than silence.

passage:
"Your phone's buzzing again," Zubin said from the top bunk. "Is that Kavin?"
"Yeah." Yash turned it face down.
"You've been ignoring him for three weeks. What happened?"
"He wants me to co-found his app. I don't want to. And every time I start to reply, it feels like I'm crushing his dream."
"So you're crushing it slowly instead."
Yash groaned. "That's harsh."
"Remember when Pranav ghosted our band? You checked your phone every hour for a month."
Yash was quiet. "Yeah. It was awful."
"So write two lines. Not an essay."
Yash picked up the phone and typed: "Kavin, sorry for the silence. I've thought about it, and I'm not going to join the app. It's a good idea, just not my path. I should have said this three weeks ago."
"Send it," Zubin said.
He sent it. Kavin replied: "Ugh, okay. Thanks for telling me. Coffee sometime anyway?"

qa.q: How long had Yash been ignoring Kavin?
Why had Yash been avoiding Kavin?
qa.a: Replying felt like crushing Kavin's dream, so Yash felt guilty and awkward about saying no.

qa.q: What made Yash's message kinder than more silence?
qa.a: It was short and honest, gave a clear no with a reason, and apologised for the delay.

qa.q: How did Kavin respond to the message?
qa.a: Disappointed ("Ugh, okay") but thankful, and still open to coffee.

grounding: Illustrates avoiding someone because a talk feels hard, and replacing silence with a short honest message.
